conventions.convention: Bicosimplicial indices satisfy p,r ≥ 0 and q ≥ a for one fixed internal lower bound. Full total degree is p+r+q, with differential δh+(-1)^pδv+(-1)^(p+r)d; diagonal total degree is n+q, with differential δdiag+(-1)^n d.
Descent uses the analytic topology of separated finite-type complex algebraic varieties, field coefficients, and F ∈ D_c^b(X;k). Proper surjections need not have acyclic, connected, or smooth fibers.

AC is assumed through the supplied resolution constructions. The bicosimplicial comparison is choice-free; the stalk contraction selects one point in one nonempty fiber, without selecting a family of sections.
Skeleton means restriction through degree N; coskeleton is the right Kan extension in augmented simplicial objects over X, with X in degree -1. A height-n bounded hypercover satisfies U = cosk_n U.

With internal lower bound a, total degree m uses p ≤ m-a; computing its cohomology and outgoing differential requires levels through m-a+1. For constant coefficients a=0. Hard cochain truncation differs from coskeleton reconstruction.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC inherited from the supplied resolutions. For a proper surjective morphism f:Y→X of finite-type complex algebraic varieties and F ∈ D_c^b(X;k), the augmented derived Cech map F→Tot_p Rf_{p*}f_p^*F is a quasi-isomorphism in the analytic topology. The normalized or unnormalized total has a uniform internal lower bound and finite diagonals. The claim commutes with arbitrary algebraic base change and coefficient morphisms, gives RΓ(X,F)≃Tot_p RΓ(Y_p,f_p^*F), and requires no fiber acyclicity, connectedness, or smoothness.

For a bicosimplicial complex K^{p,r,q} of modules over a commutative ring, with p,r≥0 and one fixed lower bound q≥a, the alternating-face total and diagonal alternating-face total are naturally chain-homotopy equivalent, with the stated Koszul signs. The comparisons preserve augmentation, permit normalization, and apply to coherent derived diagrams after a supplied functorial strict resolution. No dimensional finiteness or choice principle is required.

Assume AC inherited from the six-functor resolutions. For an augmented simplicial finite-type complex algebraic variety whose augmentation and all matching maps are proper surjective, and F ∈ D_c^b(X;k), both sheaf and global augmentation maps to the derived total are quasi-isomorphisms. There is a natural strongly convergent spectral sequence E_1^{p,q}=H^q(X_p,a_p^*F)⇒H^{p+q}(X,F). A lower bound a makes diagonals finite and determines degree m and its differential through level m-a+1. Refinements give the same comparison via X, and any two proper hypercovers have a proper common refinement. Constant coefficients give the first-quadrant sequence.

concerns.concern: Proof 4.1 says the totals for U and cosk_N sk_N U 'have the same objects and the same differentials in these three degrees.' Geometric agreement through level N does not establish literal agreement of the cited strict injective resolutions: the supplier's coinduced embedding is a product over all simplicial levels, so changing higher levels can change its low-level resolution terms. The intended cohomology comparison follows from the natural filtered comparison, whose E_1 maps are isomorphisms through level N and whose internal degrees have the common lower bound. That argument, or a truncation-compatible resolution construction, should replace the unexplained literal equality.

Verification 2.1 repeats that agreement of the hypercovers through level N makes 'the two total complexes agree in degrees m-1, m and m+1.' This inherits the strict-resolution compatibility gap in the theorem's Proof 4.1. The degree cutoff and cohomology conclusion are sound via the natural filtered comparison, but literal equality of independently constructed resolution terms has not been supplied.

alerts.finding: Fact F2 attributes proper-hypercover descent to the cited theorem 'for ... a bounded-below constructible coefficient complex F of lower bound a'. The cited thm-proper-hypercovers-compute-constructible-derived-cohomology states F ∈ D_c^b(X;k), requiring bounded coefficients, rather than arbitrary bounded-below coefficients. This broadens the cited domain without a supplied extension. The actual constant-rational application lies within the supplier's stated domain; the overstrong general citation still needs correction or justification.

seams_checked.note: The descent proofs use ordinary proper base change, exact inverse image, coherent composition, and constructible restrictions with AC retained. They do not substitute smooth base change or assert acyclic fibers.

The locally split Cech supplier is used for its general injective total models and bisimplicial composition clauses, explicitly excluding its local-section descent conclusion as a proof of proper descent. Truncation compatibility of the chosen resolutions remains the recorded proof gap.

This is a declared page prerequisite, but the assigned items make no direct citation to its equivariant results. Their ordinary constructible inputs come from the analytic and incidence pages; no stronger equivariant proposition is imported.

The proper-weights theorem's F2 changes bounded coefficients to bounded-below coefficients, as recorded in the alert. Its actual constant-rational use, finite cutoff, strong convergence, and refinement comparison are within the cited theorem. The geometric hyperresolution construction separately supplies smooth-projective refinements rather than inferring smoothness of fiber products. DHI Appendix A, Proposition A.4 and Lemma A.5, was checked at https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0205027.

The nodal-curve example uses proper descent with constant rational coefficients and finite first-quadrant diagonals. Its E_2 degeneration and weight identification are attributed jointly to the Hodge supplier, rather than inferred from the descent theorem alone.
